title: Annotatio III §.VI (2): Colloquy end — both sides measure Augsburg-article agreement and hope closer union; mutual Christian love stipulated
pass_a_gloss: (2.) That at the end of the Colloquy, either party intimates that the Colloquy held among themselves was to this end, that it might become known both how far they agreed in the Articles of the Augsburg Confession, and what hope remained of a closer union to be entered thereafter, for enlarging the true Church of Christ and extinguishing the confidence of the Pontiffs born from that Dissension of the Protestants, while meanwhile they had stipulated Christian love to one another.
pass_b_english: (2.) At the colloquy’s end both sides signal why they met: to see how far they agree in the Augsburg Confession’s articles, and what hope remains of a closer union later — to enlarge Christ’s true church and quench the papists’ confidence drawn from Protestant division — while stipulating Christian love to one another in the meantime.

Their Relation words put it thus: the colloquy was meant first to learn, in summary, whether and how far both parties are one in the twenty-eight Augsburg articles, and whether further conferences of peace-loving theologians, with Christian high authority, might raise a nearer holding-together; and both sides’ theologians would show each other Christian love going forward, faithfully and without deceit.
source_text: (2.) Quòd in fine Colloquii, utraque pars, eum in finem Colloquium inter se habitum innuit, quò innotesceret, tum quousque in Articulis Aug. Confess. consentirent, tum quae spes superesset, unionis arctioris in posterum ineundae, ad ampliandam veram Christi Ecclesiam & extinguendam Pontificiorum Fiduciam, ex Dissidio Protestantium istis subnatam, dum intereà Christianum amorem sibi invicem stipulati essent.
